posts.title: Frontier Model Convergence: Test-Time Compute and the Reasoning Wave
x_thread:
Pre-training scaling laws (Kaplan, Chinchilla) hit a soft wall in 2026. The new frontier is inference compute budget C_infer: Test-Time Compute Scaling.

Here is how Process Reward Models (PRMs), RLVR, and dynamic Monte Carlo tree search are reshaping AI architecture 🧵👇

1/ Classical LLMs emit tokens via greedy argmax sampling. They have no lookahead.

Reasoning models (o3, Claude 3.7, DeepSeek R1) treat inference as a search graph over candidate reasoning trajectories.

2/ Three pillars drive test-time compute:
- Rollout Generation: K candidate intermediate reasoning branches
- Step-Level PRM Value Scoring: Scoring intermediate logic, not just final answers
- Dynamic Backtracking: Pruning contradictions and rewinding to parent nodes

3/ Why this matters for engineering:
Accuracy scales with inference compute tokens. A 32B parameter model running 16,000 thinking tokens out-reasons a 700B parameter model answering in 200 tokens.

posts.title: Modern Agentic Systems Architecture: From ReAct Loops to Trajectory Evals
x_thread:
Unconstrained while loops and naive ReAct chains are the primary reasons 80% of agent prototypes fail in production.

Here is the 2026 Modern Agentic Operating System standard: FSM kernels, MCP 2026, and Trajectory Evals 🧵👇

1/ If your agent state is stored in raw markdown strings, it will derail after 10 turns.

Production agentic systems enforce Finite State Machine (FSM) state transitions with deterministic Zod schema validation at every tool boundary.

2/ Context Window Economics:
Naive agents dump 50,000 tokens of file contents into memory. Modern agents use progressive disclosure:
- Shallow schema discovery (<500 tokens)
- Deep tool execution only on explicit intent match
- Token compaction via AST tree pruning
3/ The golden rule of agentic reliability: Never evaluate an agent solely on the final answer. Evaluate the entire execution trajectory (tool selection, error recovery, API efficiency).

posts.title: AI Infrastructure & Hardware Economics: Blackwell, LPUs, and AI Factories
x_thread:
Inference is the new manufacturing workload. But comparing GPUs purely on $/hr rental rates is flawed procurement.

Here is the truth about NVIDIA GB200 NVL72, Groq LPUs, and the real metric: Cost per Verified Outcome 🧵👇

1/ GPUs (NVIDIA Blackwell) are bandwidth and compute monsters built for massive batch processing.

LPUs (Groq Language Processing Units) use on-chip SRAM to achieve 80 TB/s bandwidth and sub-15ms Time-to-First-Token.
2/ When an agent runs 15 multi-turn tool loops, 400ms GPU TTFT means a 10-second user delay. On an LPU, that same loop completes in 350 milliseconds.

3/ Enterprise procurement must optimize for:
Cost per Outcome = (Compute Cost/Hr × Latency) / Verification Pass Rate.

Hardware with higher deterministic completion rates is cheaper overall.
